promptLatex: If 100 objects are placed into 7 boxes, what is the minimum number of objects that must be in the most crowded box?
hintLatex: Use the generalized pigeonhole principle: if N objects are placed into k boxes, some box contains at least \lceil N/k \rceil objects.
So at least one box must contain 15 or more objects.
solutionLatex:
By the generalized pigeonhole principle, if N objects are placed into k boxes, some box contains at least \lceil N/k \rceil objects.

With N = 100 objects and k = 7 boxes: \lceil 100/7 \rceil = \lceil 14.2857... \rceil = 15.

Therefore, at least one box must contain at least 15 objects.

The answer is 15.
